title: Design a Video Streaming Platform (Netflix)
prompt:
Design the playback side of a subscription video service like Netflix. Subscribers on TVs, phones and browsers press play on a title from a catalogue of licensed and original content and expect quick start, no buffering, and quality that adapts to their connection.

Assume **200 million subscribers**, up to **50 million concurrent streams** at the evening peak, and a catalogue of about 20,000 titles.
clarify: Is the catalogue fixed and licensed (so we know what to pre-position), or user-generated?
What devices and DRM systems must be supported?
What is the target startup time and acceptable rebuffer rate?
Is live content in scope, or on-demand only?
How many regions, and are there regional catalogues and licence windows?
Can we place our own caching hardware inside ISP networks?

reference.requirements:
**Functional**
- Browse, pick a title, start playback, pause, seek, resume on another device
- Adaptive quality, subtitles, multiple audio tracks
- DRM-protected, region-restricted playback

**Non-functional**
- Start in ~2 s; rebuffering ratio well under 1%
- Availability higher than any single component (CDN, license server, control plane)
- Egress is the cost and the constraint: keep bytes close to viewers
- Graceful degradation: a control-plane outage must not stop streams already in progress
reference.estimation:
- Peak egress: 50M streams × 5 Mbps average ≈ **250 Tbps**
- Catalogue size: a 2-hour title across the bitrate ladder (sum ≈ 20 Mbps) is 20 Mbit/s × 7,200 s ÷ 8 ≈ **18 GB**; × 20,000 titles ≈ **360 TB**, perhaps ~1 PB with several codecs, audio and subtitle tracks. The whole catalogue is small enough to replicate to every large edge site
- Edge hardware: at 100 Gbps per appliance, 250 Tbps needs ≥ **2,500 appliances** at full load, so several thousand with headroom, spread across ISPs
- Control plane: 50M sessions sending a heartbeat about once a minute is ~830K requests/s, tiny, cheap requests next to the 250 Tbps of media; the data plane dominates by far
reference.api:
```
POST /v1/playback/start {title_id, device, capabilities} → {manifest_url, license_url, resume_pos}
GET  {cdn}/t/{title}/{profile}/manifest.mpd or .m3u8
GET  {cdn}/t/{title}/{profile}/seg-{n}.m4s
POST {license_url} {challenge} → DRM license (short-lived)
POST /v1/playback/heartbeat {session, pos, bitrate, rebuffers}
```
- The control plane authorises and picks a CDN endpoint; the data plane (segments) never touches it.
- Heartbeats every ~30–60 s persist the resume position and feed quality telemetry.
reference.data:
- Catalogue & licensing: `titles`, `availability(title, region, window_start, window_end)`, `assets(title, profile, codec, bitrate, manifest_ref)`, in a relational or document store, heavily cached.
- Viewing state: `watch_position(user, title, pos, device, ts)` in a KV store partitioned by user.
- Media objects: immutable segment files in object storage, **content-addressed by title/profile/segment**, ideal for caching forever.
- Operational data: CDN fill status per site, session telemetry in a stream pipeline.
reference.design:
```
client ─▶ control plane (auth, entitlement, steering) ─▶ manifest + license
   │
   └─▶ nearest edge appliance (in ISP / IXP) ─ miss ─▶ regional cache ─ miss ─▶ origin (object store)

encoding pipeline ─▶ origin ─ overnight fill ─▶ edge sites (popular first)
```
- **Play:** control plane checks subscription, region and licence window, picks edge endpoints from health and proximity, returns a manifest and DRM licence.
- **Stream:** the player pulls ~2–6 s segments, measuring throughput each time and switching renditions.
- **Fill:** caches are pre-populated off-peak by predicted demand rather than filled on miss at peak.
reference.deepdives:
- **Adaptive bitrate.** Per-title encoding ladders (a cartoon needs fewer bits than a car chase) with segments aligned on keyframes so the player can switch at any boundary. The player uses throughput estimates plus buffer level: start low for fast startup, ramp up, drop quickly when the buffer is below a threshold. Shorter segments react faster but add request overhead and lower compression efficiency.
- **CDN and edge strategy.** Owning appliances inside ISPs removes transit cost and keeps traffic off the internet backbone. Popularity is a steep power law and predictable (new releases), so push content to edges overnight instead of pull-through during peak; a two-tier hierarchy (edge, regional) protects origin from misses. Steering uses health, load and measured latency, with several fallback endpoints in the manifest.
- **Playback reliability.** Manifests list multiple CDNs; the player fails over mid-stream on errors. Prefetch the first segments when a user hovers a title. DRM licence calls are on the critical start path, so licence servers are regional and cached credentials are short-lived.
- **Degraded mode.** If the catalogue or personalisation is down, serve a cached static row and keep playing.
reference.wrapup:
- The data plane (edge caches) carries essentially all the load; the control plane is small but must be highly available.
- Trade-offs: push (predictive fill) vs pull, segment length, ladder size vs storage/encoding cost, one CDN vs multi-CDN.
- Next: live events, offline downloads, ad insertion, per-title encoding research.

rubric.text: Estimates peak concurrent streams, aggregate egress (hundreds of Tbps) and catalogue size, and concludes the data plane dominates
Separates control plane (auth, entitlement, steering, licence) from data plane (segment delivery)
Adaptive bitrate streaming: segmented HLS/DASH, manifest, bitrate ladder, client-side switching on throughput and buffer
Per-title encoding and keyframe-aligned segments to allow seamless switching
CDN/edge strategy: appliances inside ISPs, tiered cache hierarchy, origin shield
Pre-positioning/predictive fill of popular content off-peak rather than pull-on-miss at peak
Fast startup: low initial bitrate, prefetch, short segments, regional licence servers
DRM and licence flow, plus regional catalogue and licence-window enforcement
Resilience: multi-CDN or multiple endpoints in the manifest, mid-stream failover, graceful degradation of control plane
Resume position and telemetry (heartbeats) stored in a partitioned KV; QoE metrics (startup, rebuffer)
Immutable segment objects cached with long TTLs; no per-user data on the media path
